records.explanation: 親 here is part of the compound 君親 (ruler and parents), referring to one's parents/kin as the other difficult obligation. It is distinct from 君 (ruler). The compound 君親 is discussed in the main text where 許玄度 says 舉君親以為難. This is also referenced in the Liu annotation where 父子一本也亦不復難君親 connects the concept of father-son unity to the 君親 difficulty.
records.referent_role: parents (親) in the compound 君親

records.explanation: 諸人 refers to the various people who gave differing answers (或父或君) in the discussion about whether to save the ruler or the father.
許玄度 is the full name of Xu Xuandu, the person Jianwen converses with. He is distinct from Jianwen.
許 in the Liu annotation is a surname reference to Xu Xuandu (許玄度), the same person as in the main text. The annotation discusses Jianwen's criticism of Xu.
簡文 in the main text is a ruler title reference to Emperor Jianwen. He converses with Xu Xuandu (許玄度).
許 is a surname reference to Xu Xuandu, the same person as 許玄度. Xu speaks (云) to Jianwen.
邴原 is the full name of the person. The annotation '傳魏五官' refers to his biography, and he is the holder of the 魏五官 office. He is also referred to as 原 and 中郎將 later in the annotation.

君親 is a compositional kinship reference meaning 'ruler and parents', referring to the two categories of authority figures. The annotation compares 父子 with 君親, arguing they are fundamentally the same (一本).
魏五官 is an office title (魏's 五官中郎將). The annotation '傳魏五官' refers to the biography of 邴原 who held this office. The office title refers to 邴原 as the holder.
玄度 is the courtesy name of Xu Xuandu, referring to the same person. After Xu leaves, Jianwen remarks about 玄度 (Xu).

父子 is a compositional kinship reference meaning 'father and son', referring to the collective of father and child as one unit. The annotation contrasts 父子 (father-son) with 君親 (ruler and parents), arguing they are fundamentally the same.
羣賢 refers to a group of worthy scholars. 原 (邴原) discussed with them (甞與羣賢共論), so they are co-present but distinct from 原.
父 refers to father, contrasted with 君 (ruler) in the question 君邪與父邪. These are distinct referents being compared.
簡文 in the Liu annotation refers to the same ruler (Emperor Jianwen) as in the main text. It is a ruler title reference. The annotation mentions 簡文誚許意, indicating Jianwen criticizing Xu.

君 here is part of the compound 君親 (ruler and parents), referring to the ruler as one of the two difficult obligations mentioned by 許玄度. It refers to the ruler (簡文 as the sovereign), and is distinct from 親 (parents). The compound 君親 is discussed in the main text where 許玄度 says 舉君親以為難.
records.referent_role: ruler (君) in the compound 君親

records.explanation: 原 is the abbreviated personal name of 邴原, who is also referred to as 魏五官 and 中郎將 in the annotation.
中郎將 is the office title held by 邴原 (原). The text says 原/中郎將甞與羣賢共論, indicating 原 is the 中郎將.
君 here refers to the ruler/sovereign (君父俱病 context), contrasted with 父 (father). In the context of 君父俱病與君邪與父邪, 君 and 父 are distinct referents being compared.

After Xu had left, Jianwen spoke, marking a later moment subsequent to the conversation itself.
Jianwen's remark after Xu's departure that Xu could have avoided reaching this point, a later reflection on the prior exchange.
The annotation cites a biography of Wei's Wuguan (五官中郎將), referencing an earlier historical figure and period as background precedent.
The annotation records that the Wuguan once discussed with a group of worthies, a past event cited as precedent.
